name: Grog the Smasher
summary: The Muscle. Two hammers is just one hammer that thought ahead.

sheet.tagline: Two hammers is just one hammer that thought ahead.
sheet.childhood: Wheel Rat. Grew up under a mill, oiling gears and dodging the wheel.
sheet.profession: Slab Dragger. Hauled cut stone for a mason who never paid on time.
sheet.war: Joined the militia. Held a gate for nine days. Does not talk about day seven.
sheet.hook: A mason's crew you drank with went up the Spire last spring for the silver. Nobody came down. You would like the silver, and you would like to know.
sheet.notes: Your cloak is grey. Ordinary. Your friends can still see you.

items.name: Hammer
items.bonus: +1 Brute when you swing it at something

items.name: Black mallet
items.bonus: +1 Brute for breaking stone, doors, and idols

items.name: Shield
items.bonus: +1 to hold a line, block a gap, or catch a falling friend

items.name: Rations
items.bonus: Two meals

items.name: Rope, 50 ft
items.bonus: +1 to any climb

name: Sly Needle
summary: The Rogue. Locks are just questions asked badly.

sheet.tagline: Locks are just questions asked badly.
sheet.childhood: Desert Urchin. Learned to read a crowd before learning letters.
sheet.profession: Lock Snipe. Opened other people's doors for a fee, then for spite.
sheet.war: Gathered intel. Sold the same map to both sides, twice.
sheet.hook: A fence in town is paying triple for anything Titardinal-made. You have never seen a fence want something that badly, and that interests you more than the money.
sheet.notes: You picked a blue cloak. One hour into the tower, everyone else stops being able to see it. From the neck down you are a rumour. Ask the referee what that gets you before you rely on it.

items.name: Lock pick
items.bonus: +1 Skulker on locks, latches, and gibbet cages

items.name: Mirror
items.bonus: +1 to look around a corner without being the thing that gets looked at

items.name: Waterskin
items.bonus: +1 to endure heat, thirst, or a long climb

items.name: Sky-blue cloak
items.bonus: Nobody sees it after the first hour

items.name: Rations
items.bonus: Two meals

items.name: Twin knives
items.bonus: +1 Brute or Skulker in a knife fight

name: Professor Quill
summary: The Scholar. Every tower is an argument. This one is a bad one.

sheet.tagline: Every tower is an argument. This one is a bad one.
sheet.childhood: Book Fetch. Ran ladders in a library that would not hire you as a reader.
sheet.profession: Library Guide. Showed rich fools to the shelves they could not understand.
sheet.war: Fled. Took the rare manuscripts with you. Regret only the weight.
sheet.hook: You have read three contradictory accounts of the kastromancer Titardinal, and all three agree the tower is a spell rather than a building. You want to stand inside a sentence.
sheet.notes: You know the word kastromancy: magic written in architecture. Walking a shape casts it.

items.name: Quill and ink
items.bonus: +1 Erudite to copy a map, a rune, or a room number

items.name: Lantern
items.bonus: +1 to see anything that is not blue

items.name: Compass
items.bonus: +1 Erudite to work out which way a window actually faces

items.name: Rations
items.bonus: Two meals

items.name: A spellbook
items.bonus: Roll d6 on the caster table; it is an item, and it burns

name: Lucky Moxie
summary: The All-Rounder. Never been dropped down a hole I couldn't climb out of. Yet.

sheet.tagline: Never been dropped down a hole I couldn't climb out of. Yet.
sheet.childhood: Smoke Scrub. Swept chimneys, learned that the way out is usually up.
sheet.profession: Slab Dragger. A season on the quarry sleds; strong shoulders, ruined boots.
sheet.war: Profiteered. Bought a spyglass from a dying officer for the price of water.
sheet.hook: You have been broke in six towns. The Spire is either the seventh or the last one.
sheet.notes: Rope plus hook is two items and two bonuses. Say which one you are using and why.

items.name: Rope, 50 ft
items.bonus: +1 to any climb, +1 to lower someone down a shaft

items.name: Black mallet
items.bonus: +1 Brute for smashing

items.name: Brass spyglass
items.bonus: +1 Erudite to read a distant window number or count giants

items.name: Rations
items.bonus: Two meals

items.name: Grappling hook
items.bonus: +1 to catch a chain from a window ledge

name: Barnaby the Stout
summary: The Defender. I stand in the doorway. That is the whole plan.

sheet.tagline: I stand in the doorway. That is the whole plan.
sheet.childhood: Garden Acolyte. Raised in a temple orchard, taught to bury things properly.
sheet.profession: Pit Warden. Guarded a fighting pit; knows how big things move.
sheet.war: Joined the militia. Came home with the shield and none of the men.
sheet.hook: The Ricalu goblins buried teeth in a ring around the tower to lay the curse. You were taught what buried teeth mean. You would like to dig them up.
sheet.notes: Salt, buried teeth, and a spectral mentor who wants a favour. You are the party's superstition, and in this tower superstition is correct more often than not.

items.name: Tusk spear
items.bonus: +1 Brute, and long enough to keep a pelican at arm's length

items.name: Shield
items.bonus: +1 to block, brace a door, or shelter someone

items.name: Shovel
items.bonus: +1 Brute to dig, pry, or turn over a garbage heap

items.name: Rations
items.bonus: Two meals

name: Vesper the Shadow
summary: The Scout. I go first. I come back. Usually in that order.

sheet.tagline: I go first. I come back. Usually in that order.
sheet.childhood: Desert Urchin. Slept on roofs, learned every drainpipe in a city you can't name.
sheet.profession: Botany Priest. Read the lake's weeds for omens; the weeds have been wrong since spring.
sheet.war: Went underground. Two years by torchlight taught you to trust your hands over your eyes.
sheet.hook: The lake has gone quiet. The fish are strange. You think something in the tower is stealing from the water, and you intend to see it stop.
sheet.notes: Trusting hands over eyes is literally the correct strategy here. Once sky-blindness lands, a deliberate search by touch beats any amount of looking.

items.name: Torch
items.bonus: +1 to any Skulker roll made in the dark

items.name: Rose incense
items.bonus: +1 Erudite to speak with something that is not alive

items.name: Waterskin
items.bonus: +1 to endure heat, thirst, or a long climb

items.name: Rations
items.bonus: Two meals

items.name: Light crossbow
items.bonus: +1 Skulker at range; armour does not help

name: Pennywhistle
summary: The Hedge Wizard. It is not a real spell if it doesn't cost you something.

sheet.tagline: It is not a real spell if it doesn't cost you something.
sheet.childhood: Book Fetch. Copied a dead wizard's marginalia for bread money.
sheet.profession: Botany Priest. Blessed goat sheds, read smoke, kept the incense trade honest.
sheet.war: Joined the rebels. Set traps. Slept badly ever since.
sheet.hook: A spark of stolen starlight, carried to the top of a spell-shaped tower, grants a wish. You have one wish and you have had it for eleven years.
sheet.notes: A spellbook is not your only way to work magic. Anything you can name is: chalk, incense, a mirror, a held breath. Describe it, name it, and take the consequence when you miss.

items.name: Quill and ink
items.bonus: +1 Erudite to copy a rune or record a room order

items.name: Rose incense
items.bonus: +1 Erudite to call, calm, or bargain with a spirit

items.name: Bear trap
items.bonus: +1 to hold a doorway against something heavy

items.name: Rations
items.bonus: Two meals

items.name: A spellbook
items.bonus: Roll d6 on the caster table; it is an item, and it burns

name: Roll your own
summary: Blank sheet. Roll d6 on Childhood, Profession, and During the War.

sheet.hook: Why do you want what is at the top of the tower? One sentence.
sheet.notes: Roll d6 on each of the three tables in the module window. The first two each give +1 to an ability and an item, the third gives an item. Then take 2 rations, a cloak of your chosen colour, and one item of your choice. Cloak colour matters this session: pick blue only if you have thought about what that means after the first hour.
